title: helm(private): stabilize values schema + init hooks for upgrade/rollback compatibility
author: Arjun Patel
description:
Motivation: Private deployments have seen multiple upgrade/rollback issues caused by brittle Helm hooks, an evolving values schema, and templating that makes validation and automated rollbacks error-prone. This PR consolidates the values schema for the `redwood-private` chart, normalizes templating patterns across subcharts, and introduces idempotent initJobs + hook ordering to make upgrades and rollbacks deterministic.

What this PR does (high-level):
- Stabilizes values.yaml schema (v3 -> v3.1) with explicit block for `encryption`, `nodeSelector`, `tolerations`, and `postgres.backup` so chart consumers can rely on a consistent surface across upgrades.
- Refactors templating helpers (helpers.tpl) to remove conditional duplication and to centralize nodeSelector/toleration rendering.
- Reworks initJobs into idempotent, annotated Jobs with pre-upgrade and post-rollback Helm hooks and `helm.sh/hook-weight` ordering to avoid race conditions.
- Adds validation templates that render a `helm template --validate` friendly object for CI and a `pre-install` hook that validates KMS + Postgres init condition.
- Adds upgrade/rollback compatibility shims: when values are missing, chart will populate sane defaults rather than failing the release (helps multi-version upgrades).

Checklist: 
- [x] Values schema updated and annotated in values.schema.json
- [x] helpers.tpl refactor + unit tests for template rendering
- [x] initJobs converted to ordered hooks with idempotency markers
- [x] CI: lint, template-validate, unit tests, e2e-upgrade test passed
- [x] Manual canary upgrade tested on staging cluster (v3 -> v3.1)

Testing notes:
- Ran `helm lint` and `helm template` across subcharts (console, runtime, postgres, installer) to ensure no missing keys.
- Added CI job `helm-e2e-upgrade` that performs a staged upgrade then rollback in KinD cluster to assert hook ordering.
- Verified Postgres init job idempotency by forcing repeated installs and verifying backup initjob does not re-create existing backups.

Related tickets: ENG-4892 (values schema stabilization), ENG-5011 (upgrade automation), SUP-7721 (customer-reported upgrade failure on KMS-enabled private deploy).

Notes on backward compatibility:
- Defaulting logic ensures older releases that omit the new `encryption.kmsKeyRef` or `postgres.backup.enabled` keys will continue to install.
- Consumers are encouraged to opt-in to stricter validation by setting `valuesValidation.strict=true`.

Merge rationale: This change significantly reduces operational pain during private deployments and unlocks automated rollout/rollback testing in CI, which is a prerequisite for Dedicated/Private SLA work.

squash! helm(private): stabilize values schema + init hooks for upgrade/rollback compatibility

Consolidate values schema, refactor templating helpers, make initJobs idempotent and ordered, add CI e2e-upgrade tests.
release_notes:
- Stabilize redwood-private Helm values schema (v3.1) with encryption, nodeSelector, tolerations and postgres.backup blocks.
- Improve templating helpers to avoid conditional duplication and respect user-provided selectors.
- Convert initJobs to ordered, idempotent hooks to make upgrades and rollbacks deterministic.
- Add CI e2e-upgrade job to catch upgrade regressions earlier.
